messages:
alex: Heads up — StellarPay wants a 4‑week POC. Key constraints: fully air‑gapped on‑prem (no outbound), low‑latency streaming (websocket preferred), function/tool-calling to their internal fraud gRPC service, structured CSV/JSONL export to their SFTP, and SOC2 + KMS. Need a short checklist + rough delta pricing vs hosted. Any immediate blockers?

maria: Quick clarifying q's: 1) air‑gapped = no outbound to our control plane at all? 2) do they allow a private control plane inside their network or want fully offline bundle? 3) expected steady QPS / concurrency + p95 latency target? 4) model family preference (open Llama family ok)? :thinking:

alex: Answers: 1) Yes — strictly no outbound. 2) They want our on‑prem package with a local control plane instance inside their VPC/DMZ. 3) steady ~5 rps, spikes up to ~50 rps, p95 target <300ms for short prompts. 4) open Llama2‑style model acceptable.

samir: Air‑gapped changes the flow: we must provide an offline control‑plane bundle + model artifact tarball. For function/toolcalls to their internal gRPC, recommend deploying our local adapter binary inside their network that forwards toolcall requests to their internal service (no internet). Fallback strategy: enable local quantized small model variant for cost/latency spikes. Also note: streaming + KV cache must be configured to avoid large memory use on small infra.

maria: I can share a minimal adapter config and a streaming SDK snippet. For the WebSocket streaming path use the SDK with keepalive and backpressure handling. Example snippet: ```python
# minimal streaming client
from redwood import StreamingClient
client = StreamingClient(endpoint='wss://local-redwood:443', token='EPHEMERAL')
with client.stream(session_id='stellar-demo') as s:
    for chunk in s.recv():
        print(chunk)
```

olivia: Security notes: SOC2 + KMS onprem is doable but needs an MSA addendum + network diagram. They require tokens not stored persistently — we should use ephemeral tokens sourced from their KMS (HSM) or customer‑provided KMS with 5m rotation. Also need details on encryption at rest for model artifacts and audit log retention policy.

alex: Pricing ask from customer: single page estimate for a 4‑week POC including on‑prem license, model bundle, engineering support days, and any infra/ops costs. Can someone give a ballpark we can present tomorrow?

samir: Ballpark (for presales quoting): on‑prem POC license = $40k flat (one‑time) + model bundle transfer $3k, eng time ~8 eng‑days (SE + infra + eng runtime) — translate eng days to ~ $12k in professional services. Expect extra for overnight build of the local adapter (~2 additional days) if we need custom work. If we compress scope (use our containerized adapter + rulebook + no custom tool transformation) we can shave ~30%.

maria: I'll draft a week‑by‑week POC plan (fast path + full path) and a checklist for security + network items. Fast path suggestion: 1) provide containerized adapter that connects to local gRPC (no outbound), 2) use our offline model bundle, 3) demo streaming + function stub with synthetic data, 4) swap in customer tool endpoint for final test. If that works I'll send a handoff doc and the adapter config by EOD.

olivia: I'll attach the standard on‑prem security addendum and a skeleton network diagram for them to fill out. Link (internal): https://redwood.internal/legal/onprem-addendum — share with legal. Also tagging infra for required firewall port list: @deploy‑bot please publish port/host checklist.

deploy-bot: infra checklist posted: https://redwood.internal/infra/onprem-ports (internal).

alex: Thanks team. One urgent ask — can someone share a minimal function‑call stub (local) we can demo in 48h so customer's devs can see the flow? They want to see tool invocation + streaming output in a live demo.

samir: Minimal runbook + quickstart stub below (can demo immediately): ```bash
# run local adapter that exposes toolcall endpoint to the runtime
./redwood-adapter --listen 127.0.0.1:50051 --mode local --allow-unauthenticated --tool-schema ./fraud_tool.yaml
# start a containerized offline control plane (already baked for presales)
docker run -p 443:443 redwood/onprem-controlplane:presales --config ./presales-config.yaml
# sample client to trigger a function call over stream (pseudo)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer EPHEMERAL" -N \
  -d '{"input":"check payment 123","stream":true,"tool_call":"fraud_check"}' \
  https://local-redwood/api/v1/generate
```

maria: Perfect — I'll package that into the demo repo with a short README and the adapter config. Alex — I'll DM you the link once it's ready.

alex: Awesome. If we can get the stub + one‑page estimate + security addendum tomorrow morning we can keep the kickoff this week. Appreciate it. :rocket:
